3-11.caveats: Only one laboratory study exists, and its participants were healthy young adults. If you can’t fall asleep, there’s no need to force it; there’s no research showing any benefit from simply lying down with eyes closed for 10 minutes. Naps longer than an hour have been linked to higher mortality and increased risk of coronary heart disease — see Section 2, Item 38 (keep naps under 30 minutes).

3-18.sources: Noetel M et al. (2024). Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. BMJ. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-075847>; Karyotaki E et al. (2021). Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Depression: A Systematic Review and Individual Patient Data Network Meta-analysis. JAMA Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2020.4364>; Tele-MANAS, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://telemanas.mohfw.gov.in/>; Press Information Bureau, National Tele Mental Health Programme. <https://pib.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
3-18.benefit: This meta-analysis combined data from 218 randomized controlled trials involving 14,170 participants; the control group performed other activities. Compared with them, walking or running lowered depression scores by g = -0.62 (95% CI -0.80 to -0.45). Yoga produced g = -0.55 and strength training g = -0.49; higher intensity further improved outcomes. Pooled data from multiple light‑therapy studies showed an effect size of 0.84 (0.60–1.08) for seasonal depression and 0.53 (0.18–0.89) for non‑seasonal cases. Another analysis aggregated individual‑patient data from various studies on internet‑based cognitive‑behavioral therapy; both self‑guided and therapist‑supervised programs outperformed controls, with therapist guidance yielding better results for moderate‑to‑severe depression (PHQ‑9 score >9). The 14416 (Tele-MANAS) hotline provides nationwide psychological support round the clock, every day.

3-19.title: Treat police officers, doctors, and bank tellers as rule‑following workers, not as archetypes: paperwork and deadlines — not emotions — drive results.
3-19.cost: No expense involved. You only need to adjust your expectations and the sequence of actions. The first step is to resist the urge to “convince the other party with logic.”
3-19.inPlainWords: Children tend to think “police exist to catch bad guys; doctors exist to heal people.” Adults should instead view these professionals as employees bound by job rules, paperwork, deadlines, and oversight. How friendly they are has little bearing on whether your task gets done or how quickly. What matters is obtaining receipts, noting deadlines, and filing appeals through proper channels — not winning an intellectual debate.
3-19.benefit: Switching to this approach means moving from “pleading, getting angry, and reiterating your grievances” to “handling paperwork, tracking deadlines, and appealing via official routes.” The time saved comes from eliminating endless back-and-forth discussions and mental re-processing. This is a one-time mindset shift rather than a daily time-saving trick. The appeal routes are the concrete checkpoints: each one is written into the rules and produces a document you can point to, rather than being decided at the counter. Take the police: under section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 the officer in charge must register a first information report when you report a cognisable offence, and give you a copy free of cost; if the station refuses, section 173(4) lets you send the substance of the information in writing to the Superintendent of Police, who must investigate or direct an investigation, and if that fails you can apply to the magistrate, who may order an investigation under section 175(3). What you get is a documented route with a dated record at each step.
3-19.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
3-19.caveats: Grade C is assigned because there is no scholarly source supporting the premise that “many people treat front-desk staff as archetypes rather than ordinary workers.” The only evidence lies in the rules themselves: paperwork, acknowledgement and appeal mechanisms are explicitly codified. The police route summarised here is the one in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, set out in Chapter 8, Rule 39: a right to have a cognisable offence registered and a copy given free of cost, and a route to the Superintendent of Police under section 173(4) and then to the magistrate under section 175(3). It does not fix a schedule for the investigation, so treat any deadline you are quoted at a counter as something to confirm in the statute rather than assume. This entry does not promise to “guarantee success” by following the rules, nor does it address “unfriendly attitudes” on the part of officials. It merely shifts expectations and the initial course of action. The same logic applies to bank tellers and government service windows: their actions are documented, subject to review, and accountable for errors. Therefore, the proper steps are to keep receipts, request written confirmations, and file complaints through official channels — rather than speculating about whether someone might “take advantage” of you. Legitimate priorities are laid out in law; for example, emergency care is allocated based on medical severity, not on first-come-first-served order (see Chapter 24, Rule 8 on triage). If you wish to thank a doctor who helped you, send a thank-you letter or leave a satisfaction rating as described in Chapter 24, Rule 11. Offering gifts to law-enforcement personnel to “get better service” constitutes bribery, a crime with severe statutory penalties (see Chapter 8, Rule 40). Any obvious discrimination should be reported and monitored, not imitated as an unwritten norm.

3-25.cost: A strip of over-the-counter ibuprofen costs a few tens of rupees, taken only during symptomatic days. If clinical evaluation is required, an outpatient consultation and pelvic ultrasonography take half a day and the usual consultation fee.

3-27.cost: Involves consultation at a sleep center, pulmonology, or ENT clinic. Diagnostic polysomnography (overnight sleep study) is conducted in-hospital or via home sleep apnea testing devices. For moderate-to-severe disease requiring continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), buying a CPAP machine is a large out-of-pocket purchase — tens of thousands of rupees, before the mask and the filters. The primary hurdle is behavioral persistence: wearing a nasal or oronasal mask nightly takes weeks to adapt, and many patients discontinue use after a few hours per night.

3-20.title: Don’t make “how others are doing” a daily habit: set limits on apps that show peers’ updates or turn them off
3-20.cost: This costs nothing. Setting time limits or deactivating an account takes just a few minutes. The real challenge is resisting the urge to open these apps again later on.
3-20.inPlainWords: People who habitually compare themselves to others online tend to feel worse emotionally and have lower self‑esteem. Pooled clinical findings show a consistent correlation between upward social comparison and poorer psychological outcomes. Correlation does not equal causation, but randomized trials back this link: after four weeks without Facebook, participants reported a slight rise in happiness. Another study limited three major platforms to 10 minutes per day; after three weeks, loneliness and depression both declined. The trade‑off? Knowledge of current events also dropped during those four weeks of abstinence.
3-20.benefit: The combined results of 54 independent studies — 94 effect sizes and a total N of 36,583 — analyzed via a three‑level random‑effects model reveal that upward social comparison correlates with poorer mental health (average r = 0.330, 95% CI 0.289–0.370). Specific effects include higher fear of negative evaluation (r = 0.438), anxiety (0.382), depression (0.306), lower happiness (0.268) and lower self‑esteem (0.263). Life satisfaction increased by 0.12 standard deviations, while happiness rose by 0.08 standard deviations. Age, cultural background and data collection year do not alter this link. In a randomized trial of 2,743 U.S. Facebook users, 61% would accept a four‑week suspension at a cost of under $102; those in the suspension group gained 0.09 standard deviations in overall life satisfaction. Compared with typical psychological interventions (which raise happiness by ~0.34 SD and cut depression by ~0.23 SD), this effect is roughly 25–40% of that magnitude. Even after the trial ended, former suspension users still spent 12 fewer minutes per day on Facebook. A smaller trial of 143 college students showed similar benefits after limiting three platforms to 10 minutes daily. Additionally, knowledge of current affairs declined by 0.19 standard deviations, and political polarization fell by 0.16 standard deviations as a result of reduced app usage.
3-20.sources: Lei Y, Hu S, Sun Y, Zheng L (2026). "Looking up" linked to feeling down: a meta-analysis of online upward social comparison and psychological maladjustment. Frontiers in Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1825169>; Allcott H, Braghieri L, Eichmeyer S, Gentzkow M (2020). Welfare Effects of Social Media. American Economic Review, 110(3), 629–676. <https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20190658>; Allcott H, Braghieri L, Eichmeyer S, Gentzkow M (2019). The Welfare Effects of Social Media. NBER Working Paper No. 25514 (The specific numbers quoted in this article are verified verbatim in this edition, and the published abstract does not include numbers). <https://www.nber.org/papers/w25514>; Hunt MG, Marx R, Lipson C, Young J (2018). No More FOMO: Limiting Social Media Decreases Loneliness and Depression. Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology, 37(10), 751–768. <https://doi.org/10.1521/jscp.2018.37.10.751>
3-20.caveats: The correlation findings merely indicate that these patterns tend to appear together; they do not prove causation. The undergraduate trial involved only 143 subjects, limiting its statistical power. Overall effect sizes remain modest, so cutting off these apps alone will not resolve all emotional issues. This advice targets usage aimed at monitoring how others are faring; it does not apply to staying in touch with family, seeking information or job hunting. If strict limits prove hard to maintain, start by disabling push notifications, “people you may know” suggestions and homepage recommendations. For broader screen‑time management, see sections 4.15 and 4.16 (hard caps on short‑video apps and scrolling news). When feeling down, consider the actions outlined in section 19 (exercise, sunlight and regular sleep). For those seeking identity through purchases, see section 6.23; those striving to “move up a social rung” should review section 6.24.
